To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the data pushing logic can minimize the latency without increasing the incompleteness of synchrophaser networks; 2) the proposed bad data detection algorithm can detect the intentional or unintentional attacks and can be adopted as a countermeasure against the delay attack; 3) the proposed synchrophasors extraction algorithm can be implemented in real time; 4) the proposed protection scheme based on synchrophasores can detect the fault and identify the faulty line in real time

we propose and validate a new data pushing algorithm able to minimize the data latency without increasing data incompleteness, we propose and validate an algorithm to detect and remove intentional or unintentional faulty PMU measurements, we show that a delay attack can be forged and undetected by the state of the art algorithms, and we show that the GECN voltage control mechanism is able to maintain the voltage level within predefined thresholds
the proposed synchrophasors network architecture and data pushing logic are able to minimize the data latency, while maintaining high data completeness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of synchrophaser networks in order to enable their use as a reliable tool for the protection and control of power grids.
the development and validation of resilient and reliable synchrophasors networks for the real time monitoring, protection and control of power grids.
the development of resilient synchro-phasor networks for real-time monitoring, protection and control of power systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this thesis provides a complete framework for the design and validation, from theory to practice, of synchrophaser networks.
, by leveraging the proposed resilient synchrophsor networks, it is possible to develop applications that can improve the operation of power transmission and distribution systems.

this thesis provides a contribution to the state of the art in the area of synchrophaser networks by proposing a new data pushing technique and a new bad data algorithm, and by validating the IEEE C37.18 Class P Std compliant phasor extraction algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to enable the real time protection, monitoring and control of power grids with PMU measurements, we need resilient synchrophaser networks that can be designed by adopting the proposed techniques.

we have designed and validated a resilient synchrophsor network able to operate in the real field, and we have shown the potentiality of this technology for the real time monitoring, protection and control of power grids.

we have designed, implemented, validated and tested a complete synchrophasors network architecture, able to provide system operators with accurate and timely information on the state of the grid, and to enable them to control and protect it.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by leveraging the accurate knowledge of system state provided by synchrophasors, the real time operation of power grids can be enhanced by means of protection and control mechanisms that can be deployed in real fields.

synchrophasors can provide a reliable and timely source of information for the protection and control of power networks, provided that the network architecture is designed to be resilient to cyber attacks and bad data.
the synchrophasors technology is able to provide the system operators with a level of awareness and automation that can be exploited to operate power grids in an efficient way.
